correctness.rationale: Condition on the endpoint labels (a,b) of the bridge. On the a side, a=3 protects all internal vertices; a=2 leaves only assignments with at least one zero and no internal 2 or 3 to delete. For a=0 or 1, internal validity requires a 3, two 2s, or one 2 and all remaining internal labels 1. The last case protects a=1 already, but protects a=0 only when b≥2. These give exactly the four matrix rows including the exceptional terms in G_n and J_n. The two sides involve disjoint choices conditioned on (a,b), so the weight exponents add and the sum of the products is tr(M_n²). For n≥4, a side weighing at most 2 necessarily leaves an undefended internal zero. A side of weight 3 without a 3 has either one 2 and one 1 (leaving an undefended internal zero) or only 1s and 0s (no defender for any internal vertex). Thus each side must contain one 3 at weight 6, giving n² choices. Fresh direct adjacency enumeration over all labelings for n=2 and 3 in /workspace/branches/769a392d-55ad-4d41-9a0d-d72547d36996/reproduce_barbell.py confirmed every coefficient: 114 and 2325 valid functions, with leading terms 4x⁵ and 13x⁶ respectively. The frozen verifier and recorded output were inspected, not executed; the independent finite test supports the boundary cases, not the all-n proof.

value.rationale: A barbell is a natural first case of two dense blocks interacting through a cut edge. The polynomial gives all feasible weights and multiplicities, not just an optimization number; it identifies the extra tied optima at n=3 and the rigid one-3-per-block classification from n=4 onward. These exact coefficients and boundary layers are useful for evaluating counting methods and for comparison with other glued-clique graphs.
